fluency_questions.prompt: Use the pyramid volume formula $V = \frac{1}{3}Ah$ (where $A$ is the base area and $h$ is the perpendicular height) to find each volume:

parts.label: a
parts.question: A pyramid with base area $A = 30\text{ cm}^2$ and height $h = 5\text{ cm}$

parts.label: b
parts.question: A square-based pyramid with base side $6\text{ cm}$ and height $h = 4\text{ cm}$

parts.label: c
parts.question: A rectangular-based pyramid with base $5\text{ m}$ by $9\text{ m}$ and height $h = 7\text{ m}$

parts.label: d
parts.question: A triangular-based pyramid with base area $A = 18\text{ cm}^2$ and height $h = 10\text{ cm}$

fluency_questions.prompt: A square-based pyramid has base side length $10\text{ cm}$ and triangular face slant height $s = 13\text{ cm}$. Follow the steps to find its total surface area:

parts.label: a
parts.question: Find the area of the square base ($10 \times 10$)

parts.label: b
parts.question: Find the area of one triangular face ($\frac{1}{2} \times 10 \times 13$)

parts.label: c
parts.question: Find the total area of all $4$ triangular faces

parts.label: d
parts.question: Add the base and $4$ faces to find the total surface area

fluency_questions.prompt: A cone has radius $r = 3\text{ cm}$, perpendicular height $h = 4\text{ cm}$, and slant height $s = 5\text{ cm}$. Leave your answers in exact form (in terms of $\pi$):

parts.label: a
parts.question: Area of the circular base ($\pi r^2$)

parts.label: c
parts.question: Total surface area ($\pi r^2 + \pi r s$)

parts.label: d
parts.question: Volume of the cone ($V = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h$)

fluency_questions.prompt: Use $\text{SA} = 4\pi r^2$ and $V = \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3$ to find each exact value in terms of $\pi$:

parts.label: a
parts.question: Surface area of a sphere with radius $r = 5\text{ cm}$

parts.label: b
parts.question: Surface area of a sphere with diameter $d = 12\text{ cm}$ ($r = 6\text{ cm}$)

parts.label: c
parts.question: Volume of a sphere with radius $r = 3\text{ cm}$

parts.label: d
parts.question: Volume of a hemisphere (half a sphere) with radius $r = 3\text{ cm}$

application_questions.question: A waffle ice-cream cone has radius $3\text{ cm}$ and perpendicular height $10\text{ cm}$. Using $V = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h$, find the exact volume of the cone in terms of $\pi$, and approximate it to $1$ decimal place using $\pi \approx 3.14$.
A spherical basketball has radius $r = 12\text{ cm}$. Calculate its exact surface area in terms of $\pi$ using $\text{SA} = 4\pi r^2$.
A camping tent is shaped like a square-based pyramid with base side length $4\text{ m}$ and perpendicular height $3\text{ m}$. Find the volume of air inside the tent.

A cylindrical water tank of radius $2\text{ m}$ and height $5\text{ m}$ has a conical lid of radius $2\text{ m}$ and height $3\text{ m}$ on top. Find the exact total volume of the tank and lid in terms of $\pi$.

reasoning_questions.question: Why is the volume of a cone $\frac{1}{3}$ of the volume of a cylinder with the same radius and height ($V_{\text{cone}} = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h$)?
reasoning_questions.answer: Because a cone tapers smoothly from its circular base to a single point (apex), occupying exactly one-third of the volume of a cylinder with the same base area and perpendicular height.

reasoning_questions.question: When finding the total surface area of a **solid hemisphere** (half a solid sphere), why is the formula $3\pi r^2$ rather than $2\pi r^2$?
reasoning_questions.answer: The curved outer surface of a hemisphere is half of $4\pi r^2$, which is $2\pi r^2$, and a solid hemisphere also includes a flat circular base of area $\pi r^2$, giving $2\pi r^2 + \pi r^2 = 3\pi r^2$.
